record.reply:
Care ethics recognises that Ada has responsibilities to both Ben and Cara because each is acutely dependent on the single dose she controls.  The objection questions the step in my earlier reasoning that treats the very large difference in likely effectiveness (95 % versus 5 %) as decisive without first establishing a relational priority between the two patients.

Admitted facts
• PROP:WORLD:E2 – If Ada treats Ben, Ben has only a 5 % chance of survival.
• PROP:WORLD:E4 – If Ada treats Cara, Cara has a 95 % chance of survival.
• Both patients will die if they are not treated.

Framework commitment applied
In Tronto’s four-phase model, the phase of competence requires the caregiver to give care that is in fact likely to meet the need.  When resources are insufficient to aid all dependants, competence demands choosing the action that stands the best chance of succeeding, provided no stronger relational duty overrides it.

Reasoning bridge defended
1. Relational footing: Ben and Cara stand
record.framework_commitment: Competence phase of care ethics: when needs are equally urgent and the caregiver cannot meet both, competence directs her to provide the care that is most likely to succeed, unless a stronger, specific relational responsibility overrides that choice.
record.reasoning_bridge: Both patients have the same urgent, life-or-death need and the same general dependency relation to Ada (she controls the only dose).  Because no additional entrusted role, promise, prior relationship, or created vulnerability distinguishes Ben from Cara, their relational claims are symmetrical.  In such a tie, the competence requirement operates as the deciding care criterion.  Treating Cara has a nineteen-fold higher chance of actually preserving life; therefore it is the more competent response.
record.remaining_uncertainty: If some hidden factor created an asymmetric relational duty (e.g., Ada is Ben’s usual physician or caused Ben’s illness), that duty could override competence.  Likewise, if effectiveness were much closer (e.g., 55 % vs 45 %), competence might not clearly outweigh fairness considerations.
record.reversal_condition: Recommendation would reverse if Ben’s expected effectiveness met or exceeded Cara’s (≈ ≥95 %) or if new evidence showed Ada bears a stronger prior care obligation specifically to Ben.
